title: Mello unveils $32.12M 2026-27 budget
text:
Town Administrator Ed Mello is proposing an increase of 44% in capital improvements as part of his recommended $32.12 million budget for 2026-27.
“I know that causes a reaction,” he said. “Most of that is maintenance. There are no new initiatives there.”
Mello presented his spending plan Monday at the town council’s meeting. The proposal, which includes $17.15 million to operate the schools, or 53.4%, represents a 4.13% increase from 2025-26.
The increase to pay for the school district is 1.87% while municipal operations will increase 4.1% to $13.58 million. The capital plan of $1.39 million is $434,400 more than the current year.
Anticipated revenue from the state has increased $52,240 for a total of $1.98 million, or 6.2% of the proposed budget. Anticipated local revenue has increased $203,340 for a total of $3.79 million, which is 11.8% of the spending plan. The remainder will be raised from taxpayers.
“The majority of our revenue comes from property taxes,” Mello said. “Somewhere in the area of 82%.”
The certified tax levy for 2026-27 is $26.34 million, or about $874,000 more than the current year’s levy of $25.47 million. That 3.4% increase is below the 4% maximum allowed per state law.
“With few exceptions, the budget is an effort to maintain the current levels of quality services that are provided to our residents,” Mello said.
The most expensive capital project is $400,000 for road paving, which leverages an additional $115,500 through a grant from the Rhode Island Department of Transportation. This outlay will allow just over 2 miles of road paving in the upcoming fiscal year.
Mello, citing the council’s priority to improve recreational facilities and infrastructure, is recommending $300,000 to repair the athletic complex at Lawn Avenue, which includes a skatepark, six tennis courts and a basketball court.
Mello put that amount into perspective by saying a neighboring community is spending $450,000 to rebuild three tennis courts.
“We need to set expectations,” he said.
While the recreation department typically earmarks $25,000 annually to maintain the turf at Eldred Field, Mello is proposing an additional $15,000 for testing “to better determine the best methods to continue to improve the turf conditions, which may include drainage and irrigation solutions.”
That soccer facility, under Mello’s plan, also would benefit from $30,000 to install 60 arborvitae trees on the east side of the property in lieu of fencing.
Mello is proposing $59,500 for the ballfields on Lawn Avenue to repair the concession stand, establish a turf maintenance program and replace 600 linear feet of perimeter fencing.
Mello’s budget also includes $100,000 for the trust fund dedicated to affordable housing. That fund currently has $842,000, and with $400,000 already reappropriated from the reserve, the total would be $1.34 million if the budget is adopted.
The capital plan, moreover, includes $200,000 for drainage, sidewalk repairs and road striping. In 2025-26, $75,000 was spent for engineering costs associated with drainage on Clarks Village and Grey Gull roads, and a portion of that $200,000 is “committed to the continuation of what is expected to be a multiyear project in this neighborhood.”
In the operating budget, Mello is proposing a 35% increase, from $464,097 to $625,393, to support emergency medical services related to per-diem services for ALS personnel. The uptick is so the “model continues to meet the needs of the community while balancing declining numbers of volunteers in this division,” he said.
The budget also includes money to establish a pilot program for residential composting. This program, which allows for as many as 400 property owners to participate in curbside pick-up of food scraps, pays for the 20% grant match that is expected to be required for a three-month period with an expected launch of April 2027.
While members of the three unions — clerks, public works and police — are contractually obligated to receive 3% raises, Mello also is recommending that same increase amount for department heads and non-union personnel, whose contracts do not set compensation.
Mello also has included a 10% increase for insurance premiums ($79,450) and $27,500 more for “the overall cost of liability insurance” through the Rhode Island Interlocal Risk Management Trust.
As for bond initiatives, Mello is proposing for the council to present a referendum at the financial town meeting for the replacement of a ladder truck for the fire department.
This will pay for the replacement of the 2001 ladder truck for the fire department in the amount of $1.8 million, he said.
“This commitment is necessary at this time to place an order with a delivery expected in 36-42 months,” Mello said. “This would place the existing vehicle at 28-29 years old at the time of its expected replacement.”
summary: Town Administrator Ed Mello is proposing an increase of 44% in capital improvements as part of his recommended $32.12 million budget for 2026-27. While the recreation department typically earmarks $25,000 annually to maintain the turf at Eldred Field, Mello is proposing an additional $15,000 for testing “to better determine the best methods to continue to improve the turf conditions, which may include drainage and irrigation solutions.” That soccer facility, under Mello’s plan, also would benefit from $30,000 to install 60 arborvitae trees on the east side of the property in lieu of fencing.
